title: Script a Disk Usage Alert in Bash

scenes.line1: How do you script a disk alert?
scenes.say: How do you write a script that warns you when disk space is running out? Would your script actually catch the problem?

scenes.label: Parsing
scenes.sub: Disk alerts test loops, parsing, and exit codes.
scenes.say: Disk usage alert scripts test your ability to parse output, use loops, and handle exit codes—all in one go.

scenes.title: Disk usage warning
scenes.say: Run your script with a threshold. It warns you if any filesystem is over the limit, showing the mount point and free space.

scenes.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
THRESHOLD=${1:-85}
rc=0
while read -r fs size used avail pct mount; do
  p=${pct%\%}
  if (( p >= THRESHOLD )); then
    echo "WARN $mount at ${p}% ($avail free)"
    rc=1
  fi
done < <(df -P -h -x tmpfs -x devtmpfs | tail -n +2)
exit $rc
scenes.say: This is the core. It checks each filesystem, compares usage to your threshold, and returns a non-zero exit code if any are too full.

scenes.question: What does exit code 1 mean here?
scenes.right: At least one filesystem exceeded the threshold.
scenes.say: Interview trap: What does exit code one mean here? It's not just success or failure. It signals that at least one filesystem is over your threshold.
